newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco offers nine hotels for sale.
newsitem.headline: Morocco offers nine hotels for sale.

text.p: Morocco on Monday offered for sale nine hotels at a total minimum price of 95.9 million dirhams ($11 million), a privatisation ministry spokesman said.
Most of the hotels are in the south, including the tourist city of Marrakesh. Two are in Chefchaouen and Oujda, respectively in the north and east, and one in the Atlantic port city of Casablanca.
The nine hotels have a total of 813 bedrooms. The highest minimum asking price is 24.5 million dirhams for Les Almoravides, a four-star 107-bedroom hotel in Marrrakesh.

Six of the hotels are classed as four star and one as three star. Two of them, one in Casablanca and the other in Oujda on the Morocco-Algerian border, have been closed for six and three years respectively.
Morocco plans to have completed the sale of 114 companies and hotels by 1998. It has already sold stakes in 46 enterprises, including at least 18 hotels, since privatisation started in November 1993.
Offers close at midday on January 10, 1997.
